hero.title: Start in Chengdu. Go beyond.
hero.subtitle: Small-group journeys into Tibetan culture and the wild landscapes of Western China.

expect.label: Beyond the postcard
expect.title: Not all of China is what you expect.
expect.text: Most travelers see cities. We take you further — into places where cultures shift, landscapes open, and the journey becomes the destination.

route1.name: Chengdu Tibetan Walking Tour
route1.tagline: Tibetan culture hidden inside the city
route1.description: A two-hour introduction to Tibetan culture hidden inside the city — temples, tea houses, and living traditions most visitors never find.

itinerary.title: Meet & Greet
itinerary.desc: Meet at Gaoshengqiao Metro Station Exit G. Get to know your guide and fellow travelers.

itinerary.title: Tibetan Quarter Walk
itinerary.desc: Stroll through Chengdu's most authentic Tibetan neighborhood — temples, prayer wheels, traditional dress, and daily life woven together in the city.

itinerary.title: Tibetan Tea & Snacks
itinerary.desc: Step into a traditional Tibetan tea house. Taste authentic butter tea or sweet tea alongside Tibetan snacks, while listening to stories of the plateau.

itinerary.title: Tibetan Guozhuang Dance
itinerary.desc: Watch a traditional Guozhuang circle dance performance — the rhythm and warmth of highland culture. Return to the meeting point afterward.

route2.name: Highland Roads & Temple Views
route2.tagline: Escape the city into Sichuan's highlands
route2.description: Escape the city and explore highland roads, ancient temples, and mountain panoramas across the Tibetan plateau's eastern edge.

days.title: Chengdu → Kangding
days.desc: Depart Chengdu in the afternoon, cross the Erlang Mountain Tunnel via the Yakang Expressway, and arrive in Kangding — capital of Ganzi Prefecture — by evening. Stroll along the Zheduo River and soak in the Tibetan atmosphere of this legendary gateway town.

days.title: S434 · Muya Monastery · Yala雪山 → Xinduqiao
days.desc: Take the stunning Provincial Road 434 north — quieter and more scenic than the main G318. Visit Muya Monastery, where golden roofs and crimson walls frame snow peaks and grasslands. Stop at the Yala Snow Mountain viewpoint to face the majesty of this sacred peak. Arrive in Xinduqiao by dusk — known as 'photographer's paradise' for its dreamlike play of light on Tibetan villages and poplar forests.

days.title: Zheduo Pass → Chengdu
days.desc: Cross Zheduo Pass (4,298m) — the first major pass on the Sichuan-Tibet highway — surrounded by prayer flags and snow peaks. Continue via Kangding back to Chengdu, arriving in the evening.

days.title: Chengdu → Kangding
days.desc: Depart Chengdu in the afternoon, cross the Erlang Mountain Tunnel via the Yakang Expressway, and arrive in Kangding by evening. Stroll along the Zheduo River and soak in the Tibetan atmosphere.

days.title: S434 · Muya Monastery · Yala雪山 → Xinduqiao
days.desc: Take the stunning Provincial Road 434 north. Visit Muya Monastery — golden roofs and crimson walls against snow peaks. Stop at the Yala Snow Mountain viewpoint. Arrive in Xinduqiao by dusk, where light and shadow paint the Tibetan villages and poplar groves.

days.title: Tagong Grasslands · Bamei → Zhonglu Tibetan Village
days.desc: Morning walk on the Tagong Grasslands, where Muya Golden Pagoda frames Yala Snow Mountain. Continue through Bamei into Danba county. Arrive at Zhonglu Tibetan Village — a thousand-year-old Gyalrong settlement of watchtowers, pear blossoms (in spring), and terraced fields. Explore ancient watchtowers and Tibetan homes in the afternoon.

days.title: Zhonglu Village → Chengdu
days.desc: Wake up in the village as morning mist wraps around the watchtowers — Zhonglu's most magical hour. After a morning of free exploration, head back toward Chengdu via the Siguniang Mountain route (distant view from Maobiliang Pass), arriving in the evening.

days.title: Chengdu → Kangding
days.desc: Depart Chengdu in the afternoon, cross the Erlang Mountain Tunnel, and arrive in Kangding by evening. Stroll along the Zheduo River and soak in the Tibetan atmosphere of this legendary gateway town.

days.title: S434 · Muya Monastery · Yala雪山 → Xinduqiao
days.desc: Take stunning Provincial Road 434 north. Visit Muya Monastery, where golden roofs frame snow peaks. Stop at the Yala Snow Mountain viewpoint before arriving in Xinduqiao — photographer's paradise — by dusk.

days.title: Tagong · Bamei · Moshi Park → Danba
days.desc: Morning on the Tagong Grasslands — Muya Golden Pagoda and Yala Snow Mountain in one frame. Continue to Moshi Park near Bamei, where bizarre mylonite stone forests spread across the plateau like an alien landscape. Afternoon drive through the Yak Valley natural bonsai corridor to Danba.

days.title: Danba · Zhonglu Village → Siguniang Mountain
days.desc: Morning exploration of Zhonglu Tibetan Village — a thousand-year-old Gyalrong settlement of watchtowers and stone homes. Visit ancient watchtowers and meet local families. Afternoon drive to Siguniang Mountain, with a panoramic stop at Maobiliang Pass to view all four sacred peaks.

days.title: Siguniang Mountain → Chengdu
days.desc: Morning visit to Shuangqiao Valley — ride the shuttle deep into the valley, passing snow peaks, alpine meadows, and glacial lakes. Afternoon return to Chengdu via Balang Mountain and Wolong Nature Reserve, arriving in the evening.

days.title: Chengdu → Kangding
days.desc: Depart Chengdu in the afternoon, cross the Erlang Mountain Tunnel, and arrive in Kangding by evening. Stroll along the Zheduo River and soak in the Tibetan atmosphere.

days.title: S434 · Muya Monastery · Yala雪山 → Xinduqiao
days.desc: Take stunning Provincial Road 434 north. Visit Muya Monastery — golden roofs and crimson walls against snow peaks. Stop at the Yala Snow Mountain viewpoint, then arrive in Xinduqiao by dusk.

days.title: Tagong · Bamei · Moshi Park → Danba
days.desc: Morning on the Tagong Grasslands — Muya Golden Pagoda and Yala Snow Mountain in one frame. Continue to Moshi Park, where bizarre mylonite stone forests spread across the plateau. Afternoon through the Yak Valley to Danba.

days.title: Zhonglu Village — Full Day Immersion
days.desc: A full day immersed in Zhonglu Tibetan Village — watchtowers emerging from morning mist, pear blossoms weaving through stone homes. Hike to the No. 1 viewpoint for a sweeping panorama. Visit a Tibetan family for butter tea and stories of Gyalrong history. Climb the tallest ancient watchtower for sunset.

days.title: Jiaju Tibetan Village → Siguniang Mountain
days.desc: Morning visit to Jiaju Tibetan Village — 'China's most beautiful village' — where stone homes cascade down the mountainside in harmony with forest and field. Afternoon drive to Siguniang Mountain for the panoramic view of all four peaks from Maobiliang Pass.

days.title: Siguniang Shuangqiao Valley — Full Day
days.desc: A full day in Shuangqiao Valley — ride the shuttle deep into the valley from Renshenguo Meadow to Redwood Forest. Snow peaks, glaciers, alpine forests, meadows, and lakes unfold mile after mile. Optional light hikes at Bonsai Beach or beneath Budala Peak.

days.title: Siguniang Mountain → Chengdu
days.desc: One last look at Siguniang's golden sunrise (weather permitting), then return to Chengdu via Balang Mountain Tunnel and Wolong Nature Reserve, arriving in the afternoon.

route3.name: Nomad in Tibetan Area
route3.tagline: Live like a nomad on the Tibetan plateau
route3.description: Venture deep into the high grasslands of western Sichuan. Live alongside a nomadic family, learn to milk yaks, make butter tea, and sleep in a black yak-hair tent — a rare, immersive experience on the roof of the world.

days.title: Chengdu → Hongyuan Grasslands
days.desc: Depart Chengdu in the early morning, heading north along the Min River valley through Wenchuan and Li County into the northwest Sichuan plateau. As the elevation rises, the scenery outside your window transforms from city towers to alpine meadows. Arrive in the afternoon at the nomadic camp deep in the Hongyuan Grasslands. Meet your nomadic family and settle into their black tent. In the evening, gather around the stove for your first bowl of butter tea and listen to the herders' stories of the grasslands.

days.title: Full-Day Nomadic Life Immersion
days.desc: A full day of living the nomadic way. Rise early to milk yaks alongside the herders — this is how every Tibetan pastoralist begins their day. Learn to churn butter tea and knead tsampa, essential skills for life on the plateau. In the afternoon, mount a horse and ride across the vast Hongyuan Grasslands — an endless sea of grass meeting the sky, with yak herds scattered like black pearls. At dusk, help round up the yaks and bring them back to camp. Gather around the fire under the stars — in this moment, you are part of the grassland.

days.title: Hongyuan Grasslands → Chengdu
days.desc: Wake early for one last grassland sunrise — at Hongyuan, the morning sun turns the meadows gold as smoke curls from the black tent. Bid farewell to your nomadic family and begin the journey back, passing through Miyaluo and Li County before returning to Chengdu in the afternoon.

days.title: Chengdu → Hongyuan Grasslands
days.desc: Depart Chengdu in the early morning, heading north along the Min River valley through Wenchuan and Li County into the northwest Sichuan plateau. Arrive in the afternoon at the nomadic camp deep in the Hongyuan Grasslands. Meet your nomadic family and settle into their black tent. In the evening, gather around the stove for your first bowl of butter tea and listen to the herders' stories of the grasslands.

days.title: Yaks & Grasslands · Nomadic Daily Life
days.desc: A full day of living the nomadic way. Rise early to milk yaks, learn to churn butter tea and knead tsampa — the fundamentals of life on the plateau. In the morning, follow the herders onto the grasslands to find salt licks and tend the yak herds, discovering the sacred place yaks hold in Tibetan culture. In the afternoon, learn to make yak-hair rope and butter using traditional tools. At dusk, round up the yaks and bring them home. After nightfall, gather around the fire to hear the herders recount the Epic of King Gesar.

days.title: Horseback & Grasslands · Ride Free
days.desc: Today belongs to the horse. Tibetans are a people of the saddle. In the morning, saddle up and ride out with the herders to patrol the vast pastures — feel the wind rush past as you taste freedom on the open range. In the afternoon, hone your riding skills on the grasslands, progressing from a walk to a trot under the herders' guidance until you find your rhythm on horseback. If the season is right, the grasslands bloom with wildflowers in every colour — every snapshot a desktop wallpaper. In the evening, water the horses by the river and watch the sunset paint the entire grassland orange-red.

days.title: Hongyuan Grasslands → Chengdu
days.desc: Share one last breakfast with your nomadic family in the morning — tsampa, butter tea, fresh yak milk. Bid farewell to this land that has welcomed you as one of its own. Return to Chengdu via Zhegu Mountain and Miyaluo, arriving in the afternoon.

days.title: Chengdu → Hongyuan Grasslands
days.desc: Depart Chengdu in the early morning, heading north along the Min River valley through Wenchuan and Li County into the northwest Sichuan plateau. Arrive in the afternoon at the nomadic camp deep in the Hongyuan Grasslands. Meet your nomadic family and settle into the black tent. In the evening, gather around the stove for butter tea — your grassland life begins.

days.title: Yaks & Grasslands · Nomadic Daily Life
days.desc: Rise early to milk yaks, learn to churn butter tea and knead tsampa. In the morning, follow the herders onto the grasslands to find salt licks and tend the yak herds. In the afternoon, learn to make yak-hair rope and butter using traditional tools. At dusk, round up the yaks and bring them home. After nightfall, gather around the fire to hear the herders recount the Epic of King Gesar.

days.title: Horseback & Grasslands · Ride Free
days.desc: Saddle up and ride out with the herders to patrol the vast pastures. In the afternoon, hone your riding skills on the grasslands and find your rhythm on horseback under the herders' guidance. In the evening, water the horses by the river and watch the sunset paint the grassland red.

days.title: Grassland Gathering · A Day of Fortune
days.desc: This day belongs to the surprises of the grasslands. If your visit coincides with a horse-racing festival, a wedding, or a Dharma assembly — you will take part as family: wear a Tibetan robe, drink wedding wine, watch horses thunder across the range, and dance the Guozhuang deep into the night. If no major event falls on this day, join the herders in moving camp (season permitting), or learn to make traditional Tibetan yogurt and air-dried yak meat. No two days on the grasslands are the same — and the season you arrive is the finest of all.

days.title: Hongyuan Grasslands → Chengdu
days.desc: Share one last breakfast with your nomadic family in the morning, and capture the black tent, the chimney smoke, and the smiling faces of your grassland family on camera. Bid farewell to this land that has turned you from guest into family. Return to Chengdu via Zhegu Mountain and Miyaluo, arriving in the afternoon.

days.title: Chengdu → Hongyuan Grasslands
days.desc: Depart Chengdu in the early morning, heading north along the Min River valley through Wenchuan and Li County into the northwest Sichuan plateau. Arrive in the afternoon at the nomadic camp deep in the Hongyuan Grasslands. Meet your nomadic family — from this moment on, they are your grassland family. Settle into the black tent. In the evening, gather around the stove for butter tea — your nomadic life begins.

days.title: Milking · Herding · Nomadic Daily Life
days.desc: Morning lesson one: milk a yak. Master this, and you understand the rhythm of nomadic life. In the morning, follow your family onto the grasslands to herd, and learn to recognise each yak — every one of them has a name. In the afternoon, learn to churn butter tea, knead tsampa, and make yak yogurt. At night, gather around the fire and listen to father tell the epic battles of King Gesar.

days.title: Riding · Training · Gallop on the Grassland
days.desc: A full day with horses. In the morning, saddle up and walk with the herders to patrol the pasture boundaries. In the morning, learn basic riding and rein control. In the afternoon, gallop across the open grasslands — the purest joy is the wind on horseback. In the evening, go to the river to brush the horses and let them drink, watching the sunset turn their manes gold.

days.title: Craft · Food · Nomadic Skills
days.desc: Today, learn the survival wisdom of nomadic peoples. In the morning, use traditional tools to spin yak-wool yarn and braid rope for black tents — skills passed down for a thousand years. In the afternoon, work alongside the mother of the family to make air-dried yak meat and brew traditional yak yogurt. In the evening, build a fire with yak dung (the most precious fuel on the grasslands) and learn to bake Tibetan flatbread. In every step of the process lies the wisdom of survival on the high plateau.

days.title: Moving Camp · Horse Racing · Grassland Festival
days.desc: This day belongs to the surprises of the grasslands. If it falls on a horse-racing festival — you will witness a hundred horses thundering across the range, riders flying like the wind. If a wedding — wear a Tibetan robe, drink barley wine, and dance the Guozhuang for three days and three nights. If a Dharma assembly — prayer flags billow and ritual horns sound low, a feast of faith for the entire grassland. Just an ordinary day? Then drive the yaks with the herders as they move camp to the summer pasture — a day's journey, a road of scenery.

days.title: Grassland Wander · Starry Sky · Farewell Eve
days.desc: Your last full day on the grasslands. In the early morning, ride deep into the grasslands to watch the sunrise. Find a quiet hillside and sit, looking out over this land you have begun to know. In the afternoon, help the family prepare for tomorrow's farewell — perhaps make one more pot of butter tea, perhaps ride one more time. After nightfall, lie on the grassland and gaze at the stars — in Hongyuan, with no light pollution, the Milky Way hangs directly overhead.

days.title: Hongyuan Grasslands → Chengdu
days.desc: True farewells are always hard. In the morning, share one last breakfast with your family — yak milk, tsampa, butter tea. Embrace and exchange contact details — from now on, you have a home on the grasslands. Return to Chengdu via Zhegu Mountain and Miyaluo, arriving in the afternoon.

item1.title: Small groups
item1.text: No crowded buses. No flag-following. Small groups mean real conversations, flexible routes, and access to places large groups can't reach.

item2.title: Local insight, not scripted tours
item2.text: Our guides are from the communities we visit. No rehearsed commentary — just real knowledge shared naturally along the way.

item3.title: Access to real Tibetan communities
item3.text: Years of relationships open doors that tourism hasn't reached. Share tea with families, visit working monasteries, see life as it's lived.

item4.title: Flexible and personal
item4.text: Every journey adapts to the group. Weather shifts? We change the route. Someone wants to stay longer at a village? We make it work.

cta.label: Join us
cta.title: Limited spots. Real experiences.
cta.text: We keep our groups small to keep the experience real. Plan early to secure your place.
